chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Basir who said:

When a man swears three oaths while he is in the state of Ihram and he is truthful, upon him is blood (a sacrificial animal) that he must shed. And when he swears one oath while lying, he has disputed (with God), and upon him is blood that he must shed.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.جَادَلَ: He has disputed or contended (with God regarding the oath)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Sacrificial animal (usually a sheep, goat, cow, or camel) offered as expiation
key_terms.يُهْرِيقُهُ: He must shed/release (the blood of the sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Abu Basir, highlighting the juristic consensus that the state of Ihram imposes a specific sacrificial liability (*dam*) for oath violations, regardless of truthfulness or frequency. This distinction underscores the unique spiritual gravity of Ihram, where even truthful oaths carry a penalty, reflecting the principle that the sanctity of the pilgrimage state requires expiation for any binding verbal commitment that is later broken.
